To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transcriptional repression of histone H1 is mediated by an element located between -130 to -106 bp of the gene promoter.
transcription of the histone gene H1t is repressed in somatic cells by a repressor element in the proximal promoter.

a repressive element within the proximally located histone H1 promoter mediates transcriptional repression of a testis-specific histones gene in non-germinal cells and that the repression is mediated by a complex of proteins that do not bind to the repressor element in testis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for transcription of a testis-specific gene and its repression in other cell types.
transcriptional regulation of a gene encoding a protein that is essential for normal spermatogenesis.
transcriptional regulation of the histone genes in mammalian cells, particularly those expressed in germ cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

transcriptional repression of histone H1T is mediated by a complex interaction of several mechanisms including the H1t promoter RE element, the H1/ AC box, a GC-rich element, and methylation of CpGs within the H1t proximal promoter.
the testis-specific gene is repressed by several different promoter elements, and that these different mechanisms are cell-type specific and are not necessarily present in all cell types.
multiple mechanisms contribute to repression of the Ht1 gene in NIH 3Ts cells and that the mechanism mediated by RE differs significantly from that mediated by the GC rich region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multiple mechanisms contribute to transcriptional repression of histone H1 genes.
transcriptional repression of this gene is mediated by multiple elements that may be differentially regulated in different cell types.
multiple mechanisms contribute to transcriptional repression of histone H1 gene expression in non-spermatocyte cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transcription of the histone gene is repressed in most cells by multiple mechanisms and that the mechanisms differ in different cells.
multiple mechanisms of transcriptional regulation are involved in transcription of the histone gene and that the mechanisms are not necessarily conserved among species.
the H1t promoter has several distinct repressive elements that function to prevent transcription of the H1T gene in somatic cells.
